_meta.method: complete direct literal rendering; source order preserved; no explanatory paraphrase

word_for_word: कथं हन्तीत्यनेनोक्तं वधसाधनाभावं दर्शयन्नविनाशित्वमात्मनः स्फुटीकरोति नैनमिति
showing the absence of any means of killing, stated by ‘how does he kill?’, he makes the Self’s indestructibility clear with ‘this is not’
आपो नैनं क्लेदयन्ति मृदुकरणेन शिथिलं न कुर्वन्ति
waters do not moisten it; they do not soften it by making it tender
तत्र हेतूनाह अच्छेद्य इति सार्धेन
he gives the reasons in the verse and a half beginning ‘uncuttable’
निरवयवत्वादच्छेद्योऽयमक्लेद्यश्च
because it has no parts, it cannot be cut or moistened
अमूर्तत्वात् अदाह्यो द्रवत्वाभावादशोष्य इति भावः
because it is immaterial it cannot be burned; because it lacks liquidity it cannot be dried; this is the intention
अतश्च छेदादियोग्यो न भवति
therefore it is not susceptible to cutting and the rest
यतो नित्यः अविनाशी सर्वत्रगतः स्थाणुः स्थिरस्वभावः रूपान्तरापत्तिशून्यः अचलः पूर्वरूपापरित्यागी सनातनोऽनादिः
because it is eternal, indestructible, all-pervading, stable, of a firm nature, without assuming another form, unmoving, not abandoning its former form, everlasting and beginningless
किंच अव्यक्तश्चक्षुराद्यविषयः
and further, ‘unmanifest’ means not an object of the eye and the other senses
अचिन्त्यो मनसोऽप्यविषयः
‘unthinkable’ means not even an object of the mind
अविकार्यः कर्मेन्द्रियाणामप्यगोचर इत्यर्थः
‘unchangeable’ means not accessible even to the organs of action; this is the meaning
उच्यत इति नित्यत्वादावभियुक्तोक्तिं प्रमाणयति
‘it is said’ establishes as authority the statements of competent persons concerning its eternality and the rest
उपसंहरति तस्मादिति
he concludes with ‘therefore’
तदेवमात्मनो जन्मविनाशाभावान्न शोकः कार्य इत्युक्तम्
thus it has been said that grief should not arise because the Self has neither birth nor destruction
इदानीं देहेन सहात्मनो जन्म तद्विनाशेन च विनाशमङ्गीकृत्यापि शोको न कार्य इत्याह अथ चेति
now he says with ‘but if’ that even accepting birth of the Self together with the body and its destruction when the body is destroyed, grief should still not arise
अथ च यद्यप्येनमात्मानं नित्यं सर्वदा तत्तद्देहे जाते जातं मन्यसे तथा तद्देहे मृते मृतं मन्यसे
even if you always consider this Self born whenever each body is born and dead whenever that body dies
पुण्यपापयोस्तत्फलभूतयोर्जन्ममरणयोरात्मगामित्वात्
because birth and death, the fruits of merit and demerit, are regarded as going to the Self
तथापि त्वं शोचितुं नार्हसि
even then you ought not to grieve
कुत इत्यत आह जातस्येति
why? to this he says ‘of what is born’
हि यस्माज्जातस्य स्वारम्भककर्मक्षये मृत्युर्धुवो निश्चितः
because for one born, when the karma that began that birth is exhausted, death is certain, fixed
मृतस्य तत्तद्देहकृतेन कर्मणा जन्मापि ध्रुवमेव
and for one dead, birth is equally certain through karma performed in the respective body
तत्तस्मादेवमपरिहार्येऽर्थेऽवश्यंभाविनि जन्ममरणलक्षणेऽर्थे त्वं विद्वाञ्शोचितुं नार्हसि
therefore, regarding this unavoidable matter characterized by birth and death that must certainly occur, you, being wise, ought not to grieve
योग्यो न भवसीत्यर्थः
you are not fit to do so; this is the meaning
किंच देहादीनां च स्वभावं पर्यालोच्य तदुपाधिके आत्मनो जन्ममरणे च शोको न कार्य इत्याह अव्यक्तादीनीति
and further, considering the nature of bodies and the rest, one should not grieve over the Self’s birth and death conditioned by them; he says this with ‘unmanifest in the beginning’
अव्यक्तं प्रधानं तदेवादिः पूर्वरूपं येषां तान्यव्यक्तादीनि भूतानि शरीराणि कारणात्मनापि स्थितानामेवोत्पत्तेः
beings, bodies, are unmanifest in the beginning because their prior form is the unmanifest Pradhāna; their arising is only of what already exists in causal form
तथा व्यक्तमभिव्यक्तं मध्यं जन्ममरणान्तरालस्थितिलक्षणं येषाम्
their middle is manifest, characterized by the state between birth and death
अव्यक्ते निधनं लयो येषां तानीमान्येवंभूतान्येव
their end is dissolution into the unmanifest; these are simply of this nature
तत्र तेषु का परिदेवना कः शोकनिमित्तो विलापः
what lamentation is there concerning them, what wailing caused by grief?
प्रतिबुद्धस्य स्वप्नदृष्टवस्तुष्विव शोको न युज्यत इत्यर्थः
for one awakened, grief over objects seen in a dream is not appropriate; this is the meaning
कुतस्तर्हि विद्वांसोऽपि लोके शोचन्ति आत्माज्ञानादेवेत्याशयेनात्मनो दुर्विज्ञेयतामाह आश्चर्यवदिति
then why do even learned people grieve in the world? with the intention that it is only from ignorance of the Self, he states the Self’s difficulty of being known with ‘as a wonder’
कश्चिदेनमात्मानं शास्त्राचार्योपदेशाभ्यां पश्यन्नाश्चर्यवत्पश्यति
someone, seeing this Self through the instruction of scripture and teacher, sees it as a wonder
सर्वगतस्य नित्यज्ञानानन्दस्वभावस्यात्मनोऽलौकिकत्वादैन्द्रजालिकवदघटमानं पश्यन्निव विस्मयेन पश्यति असंभावनाभिभूतत्वात्
because the all-pervading Self, whose nature is eternal knowledge and bliss, is extraordinary, he sees it with amazement as though seeing an impossibility like magic, being overwhelmed by incredulity
तथा आश्चर्यवदन्यो वदति च शृणोति च
likewise another speaks of it as a wonder, and another hears of it as a wonder
अन्य कश्चित्पुनर्विपरीतभावनाभिभूतः श्रुत्वापि नैव वेद
yet another, overwhelmed by contrary notions, does not know it even after hearing
चशब्दादुक्त्वापि न सम्यग्वेदेति द्रष्टव्यम्
from the word ‘and’ it should be understood that even after speaking of it one may not know it correctly
तदेवं दुर्बोधमात्मतत्त्वं संक्षेपेणोपदिशन्नशोच्यत्वमुपसंहरति देहीति
thus, briefly teaching the difficult-to-understand truth of the Self, he concludes that it is not to be grieved for with ‘the embodied’
यच्चोक्तमर्जुनेन वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते इति तदप्ययुक्तमित्याह स्वधर्ममिति
what Arjuna said—‘trembling arises in my body and my hair stands on end’—is also improper; he says this with ‘your own dharma’
आत्मनो नाशाभावादेवैतेषां हननेऽपि विकम्पितुं नार्हसि
because the Self is not destroyed, even in killing these persons you ought not to tremble
किंच स्वधर्ममप्यवेक्ष्य विकम्पितुं नार्हसीति संबन्धः
and further, considering your own dharma, you ought not to tremble; this is the connection
यच्चोक्तं न च श्रेयोऽनु पश्यामि हत्वा स्वजनमाहवे इत्यादि तत्राह धर्म्यादिति
regarding what was said, ‘I see no good in killing my own people in battle’ and so forth, he replies with ‘than a righteous’
धर्मादनपेतान्न्याय्याद्युद्धादन्यत्
other than a battle not departing from dharma, that is, a just battle
किंच महति श्रेयसि स्वयमेवोपगते सति कुतो विकम्पस इत्याह यदृच्छयेति
and further, when a great good has come of itself, why do you tremble? he says this with ‘by chance’
यदृच्छयाऽप्रार्थितमेवोपपन्नं प्राप्तमीदृशं युद्धं सुखिनः सभाग्या एव लभन्ते
such a battle that has come by chance, unasked for, is obtained only by fortunate, blessed persons
यतो निरावरणं स्वर्गद्वारमेवैतत्
because this is an unobstructed gate to heaven
यद्वा य एवंविधं युद्धं लभन्ते त एव सुखिन इत्यर्थः
or, those who obtain a battle of this kind are themselves fortunate; this is the meaning
एतेन स्वजनं हि कथं हत्वा सुखिनः स्याम इति यदुक्तं तन्निरस्तं भवति
by this the statement ‘how could we be happy after killing our own people?’ is refuted
विपक्षे दोषमाह अथ चेत्त्वमिति
he states the fault in the contrary course with ‘but if you’
किंच अकीर्तिमिति
and further, with ‘infamy’
अव्ययां शाश्वतीम्
‘imperishable’ means lasting
संभावितस्य बहुमानितस्याकीर्तिर्मरणादतिरिच्यतेऽधिकतरा भवति
for one who is esteemed, highly honored, infamy exceeds death; it is worse than death
किंच भयादिति
and further, with ‘from fear’
येषां बहुगुणत्वेन त्वं पूर्वं संमतोऽभूस्त एव भयेन संग्रामात्त्वां निवृत्तं मन्येरन्
those by whom you were previously highly regarded for your many qualities would think that you withdrew from battle out of fear
ततश्च पूर्वं बहुमतो भूत्वा लाघवं यास्यसि
thus, having previously been highly respected, you will fall into contempt
किंच अवाच्येति
and further, with ‘unspeakable’
अवाच्यान्वादान्वचनानर्हाञ्शब्दांस्तवाहितास्त्वच्छत्रवो वदिष्यन्ति
your enemies, those hostile to you, will speak unspeakable statements, words unfit to be uttered
यच्चोक्तं न चैतद्विद्मः कतरन्नो गरीयो यद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः इति तत्राह हतो वेति
regarding what was said, ‘we do not know which is better for us, whether we should conquer them or they us,’ he replies with ‘either slain’
पक्षद्वयेऽपि तव लाभ एवेत्यर्थः
in either alternative there is gain for you; this is the meaning
